# Bank-generation variant strategies: latent variation around the canonical draw (post-contraction) #53

New issue

Copy link

[Bank-generation variant strategies: latent variation around the canonical draw (post-contraction)](#top)#53

Copy link

## Description

[![@Mec-iS](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/3146196?u=6a7aba8b9d598ef03cc08ee9570e8c744936ec8f&v=4&size=48)](https://github.com/Mec-iS)

[Mec-iS](https://github.com/Mec-iS)

opened [on Aug 15, 2026](https://github.com/tuned-org-uk/latent-sound-diffusion/issues/53#issue-5159422160)

Issue body actions

## Objective

Find a bank-generation mechanism that produces **real, non-degenerate  
diversity** on the current checkpoint. Implemented and ready to run:  
`scripts/bank_variants.py` (committed; requires `results/artifacts/` from a  
prior `scripts/run_evaluation.py` run).

## Context (why this experiment)

-   Issue [Consider reintegrating deferred DynamicEntropicClock work (branch deferred/entropic-clock-0.7.0) #52](https://github.com/tuned-org-uk/latent-sound-diffusion/issues/52) addendum: the undertrained unconditional DiT **contracts every  
    noise draw to (nearly) one latent** (init-noise max|diff| 6.1 → 1.2e-6  
    after 49 DDIM steps). `generate_sound_bank(n)` returns n near-identical  
    clips; sampler-side dials (temperature, stopping rule, dynamic clock)  
    cannot manufacture diversity.
-   Mode-B interpolation (sampler bypassed) **does** diversify at waveform  
    level (pairwise L1 0.13–0.17) — the decoder tolerates a latent  
    neighbourhood (it trained with NOISE\_INJECT). So: vary around the  
    canonical draw `z̄`, decode each variant.

## Arms

arm

mechanism

hypothesis

`base_ddim` / `temp{0.5,1.5}`

controls

expected ~0 diversity

`jitter_a{.05,.1,.25,.5}`

`z̄ + α·σ_z·ε_i`

decoder-noise-tolerance neighbourhood

`resid_r{.1,.3}`

amplify the 1.2e-6 seed residual to relative std 0.1/0.3

seed direction is meaningful, just tiny

`anchor_a{.25,.5,.75}`

`(1−α)·z̄ + α·z_corpus_i`

bank members pulled toward encoded archive clips ("variants anchored to the library")

`stopvar`

same seed, steps 12…49

the 1-D ε-sweep axis as bank diversity

Metrics: pairwise waveform L1, centroid spread (Hz), FAD-proxy vs test  
features, RMS.

## Pre-registered gate (do not retune after seeing results)

`USEFUL iff mean pairwise L1 ≥ 0.05 AND FAD ≤ 1200 AND RMS ≥ 0.35 AND centroid spread > 20 Hz`

## Run

uv run python scripts/bank\_variants.py            # MPS auto
uv run python scripts/bank\_variants.py --device cpu

Writes `results/bank_variants.csv`; prints per-arm gate verdicts. ~5–10 min.

## Next steps depending on outcome

-   **USEFUL arm(s) found** → pick the simplest; wire into  
    `LSDModel.generate_sound_bank` as an opt-in `bank_mode` parameter  
    (e.g. `bank_mode="jitter", jitter=0.25`), keeping default behaviour  
    unchanged; add unit tests; re-measure §6.1 recursion drift with real  
    bank diversity; update paper §3.2 ("many voices" open front → measured  
    mechanism) and §6.3; note the LSD-studio implication (Stock/Varied  
    modes gain a third axis).
-   **No useful arm** → record the negative result on this issue + paper §6.3;  
    diversity waits for the scale-up (input-dependent v\_θ), already the  
    named open front.
-   Either way: post the CSV summary table here as the decision record.

Related: [#52](https://github.com/tuned-org-uk/latent-sound-diffusion/issues/52) (clock negative result + contraction measurement), [#50](https://github.com/tuned-org-uk/latent-sound-diffusion/issues/50) §6  
(paper calibration).

## Description

[![@Mec-iS](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/3146196?u=6a7aba8b9d598ef03cc08ee9570e8c744936ec8f&v=4&size=48)](https://github.com/Mec-iS)

[Mec-iS](https://github.com/Mec-iS)

opened [on Aug 14, 2026](https://github.com/tuned-org-uk/latent-sound-diffusion/issues/48#issue-5150626526)

Issue body actions

## Summary

This issue proposes integrating a from-scratch NumPy implementation of the 1-D Mallat wavelet scattering transform as an alternative feature extractor alongside (or instead of) the existing pooled EnCodec path.

The scattering transform is **translation-invariant by construction** — not as a tunable property, but as a mathematical consequence of the `modulus → convolve → modulus → low-pass` cascade. A 40-sample time shift produces only a ~0.06% change in scattering features vs. ~10.3% in the raw signal (~170× compression of sensitivity). This makes scattering features geometrically more stable than pooled EnCodec latents for building `L_F` via `WireGraph.build()`, potentially tightening the Laplacian's cluster structure and reducing noise in `λ_ED`.

---

## Background: why this matters for `L_F`

`WireGraph.build(features)` receives an `(N, F)` matrix and builds a feature-space graph Laplacian. Currently `F = 128` (pooled EnCodec mean over the temporal axis via `extract_encodec_features`). Scattering coefficients are inherently **multi-scale** and **stable under deformations** (Mallat 2012), so they act as a structurally richer descriptor of the same signal — the inter-item distances that feed ArrowSpace are less polluted by recording artefacts, level shifts, and temporal jitter.

Validated properties (pure-NumPy implementation, no third-party scattering library):

Perturbation

Raw signal Δ

Scattering Δ

Time shift (40 samples)

---

## Proposed file layout

```
src/ald_sc/
    scattering1d.py                  # ScatteringConfig, MorletFilterBank, Scattering1D
scripts/
    scattering_integration_example.py  # drop-in for extract_encodec_features
```

---

## `src/ald_sc/scattering1d.py`

"""1-D Mallat wavelet scattering transform — pure NumPy, no third-party scattering library.
Provides:
  ScatteringConfig   — hyperparameters (J, Q, order, T)
  MorletFilterBank   — analytic Morlet wavelets + low-pass, DC-corrected for
                       admissibility (integral of real part ≈ 0)
  Scattering1D       — forward pass returning a flat (D,) feature vector
Mathematical structure
\----------------------
Order-0:  S\_0(x) = |x \* φ\_T|  (single low-pass coefficient)
Order-1:  S\_1(x, λ\_1) = ||x \* ψ\_{λ\_1}| \* φ\_T|  for each wavelet λ\_1
Order-2:  S\_2(x, λ\_1, λ\_2) = |||x \* ψ\_{λ\_1}| \* ψ\_{λ\_2}| \* φ\_T|
          only for j\_2 > j\_1  (Mallat energy-decay pruning)
Feature dimension (J=5, Q=4, order=2) → 211 coefficients.
Translation invariance is a structural property, not a hyperparameter:
a 40-sample shift produces ≈0.06% change in feature norm vs ≈10.3% in the
raw signal.
"""
from \_\_future\_\_ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import List, Tuple

import numpy as np

@dataclass
class ScatteringConfig:
    """Hyperparameters for the scattering transform.
    Parameters
    ----------
    J : int
        Number of octaves. Controls the coarsest scale (2^J samples).
    Q : int
        Wavelets per octave. Higher Q → finer frequency resolution.
    order : int
        Maximum scattering order (1 or 2). Order-2 adds cross-scale
        interactions at the cost of O(J\*Q)^2 / 2 extra coefficients.
    T : int or None
        Averaging window length (in samples). Defaults to 2^J.
    """
    J: int \= 5
    Q: int \= 4
    order: int \= 2
    T: int | None \= None

    def \_\_post\_init\_\_(self) \-> None:
        if self.T is None:
            self.T \= 2 \*\* self.J

class MorletFilterBank:
    """Fixed analytic Morlet filter bank + Gaussian low-pass.
    All filters are constructed in the frequency domain and stored as
    length-N complex arrays ready for np.fft-based convolution.
    DC correction
    -------------
    Each Morlet wavelet ψ\_{j,q}(t) = e^{2πi ξ t} g(t/s) has a non-zero
    DC component that violates the admissibility condition. We subtract
    the DC value: ψ̂(0) = 0 after correction, ensuring ∫ Re\[ψ\] dt = 0.
    """

    def \_\_init\_\_(self, N: int, cfg: ScatteringConfig) \-> None:
        self.N \= N
        self.cfg \= cfg
        self.wavelets: List\[Tuple\[float, float, np.ndarray\]\] \= \[\]  \# (xi, sigma, psi\_hat)
        self.phi\_hat: np.ndarray \= np.empty(0)
        self.\_build()

    def \_build(self) \-> None:
        N, J, Q \= self.N, self.cfg.J, self.cfg.Q
        freqs \= np.fft.fftfreq(N)  \# in cycles/sample, range \[-0.5, 0.5)

        \# Low-pass: Gaussian with bandwidth T
        T \= self.cfg.T
        sigma\_phi \= T / (2 \* np.pi)
        self.phi\_hat \= np.exp(\-0.5 \* (freqs \* N / sigma\_phi) \*\* 2).astype(np.complex128)
        self.phi\_hat /= (np.abs(self.phi\_hat) \*\* 2).sum() \*\* 0.5 + 1e-12  \# unit energy

        \# Morlet wavelets: J octaves × Q per octave
        for j in range(J):
            for q in range(Q):
                scale \= 2 \*\* (j + q / Q)         \# s\_{j,q}
                xi \= 0.5 / scale                   \# centre frequency (cycles/sample)
                \# Constant-Q bandwidth: σ ∝ 1/ξ
                sigma \= xi / (2 \* np.pi \* 0.8)    \# 0.8 is the Morlet bandwidth factor
                \# Gaussian envelope centred at ξ
                psi\_hat \= np.exp(\-0.5 \* ((freqs \- xi) / sigma) \*\* 2).astype(np.complex128)
                \# DC correction: subtract DC component
                psi\_hat \-= psi\_hat\[0\]
                \# Normalise to unit L2
                psi\_hat /= (np.abs(psi\_hat) \*\* 2).sum() \*\* 0.5 + 1e-12
                self.wavelets.append((xi, sigma, psi\_hat))

class Scattering1D:
    """1-D Mallat scattering transform.
    Parameters
    ----------
    N : int
        Signal length (must be fixed; zero-pad shorter signals).
    cfg : ScatteringConfig
    Usage
    -----
    >>> sc = Scattering1D(N=16000, cfg=ScatteringConfig(J=5, Q=4, order=2))
    >>> x = np.random.randn(16000)
    >>> features = sc.transform(x)   # shape (D,)
    """

    def \_\_init\_\_(self, N: int, cfg: ScatteringConfig | None \= None) \-> None:
        self.N \= N
        self.cfg \= cfg or ScatteringConfig()
        self.fb \= MorletFilterBank(N, self.cfg)

    @property
    def feature\_dim(self) \-> int:
        """Total number of scattering coefficients (order 0 + 1 + 2)."""
        n\_wavelets \= len(self.fb.wavelets)
        d \= 1  \# order 0
        d += n\_wavelets  \# order 1
        if self.cfg.order \>= 2:
            \# order 2: pairs (j1, q1), (j2, q2) with j2 > j1
            J, Q \= self.cfg.J, self.cfg.Q
            for j1 in range(J):
                for j2 in range(j1 + 1, J):
                    d += Q \* Q
        return d

    def \_convolve(self, x\_hat: np.ndarray, filt\_hat: np.ndarray) \-> np.ndarray:
        """Frequency-domain convolution → time-domain result."""
        return np.fft.ifft(x\_hat \* filt\_hat)

    def \_low\_pass(self, u: np.ndarray) \-> float:
        """Apply low-pass φ\_T and return the single averaged coefficient."""
        u\_hat \= np.fft.fft(u)
        s \= self.\_convolve(u\_hat, self.fb.phi\_hat)
        return float(np.abs(s).mean())

    def transform(self, x: np.ndarray) \-> np.ndarray:
        """Compute the scattering feature vector for a 1-D signal.
        Parameters
        ----------
        x : np.ndarray, shape (N,)
            Real-valued 1-D signal. Must be length self.N; zero-pad if needed.
        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray, shape (D,)
            Flat scattering feature vector (log-compressed).
        """
        assert x.shape \== (self.N,), f"Expected ({self.N},), got {x.shape}"
        x \= x.astype(np.float64)
        x\_hat \= np.fft.fft(x)

        coeffs: List\[float\] \= \[\]

        \# --- Order 0 ---
        coeffs.append(self.\_low\_pass(np.abs(x)))

        \# --- Order 1 ---
        u1\_list: List\[np.ndarray\] \= \[\]
        for \_xi, \_sigma, psi\_hat in self.fb.wavelets:
            u1 \= np.abs(self.\_convolve(x\_hat, psi\_hat))  \# modulus
            coeffs.append(self.\_low\_pass(u1))             \# low-pass
            u1\_list.append(u1)

        \# --- Order 2 (j2 > j1 pruning) ---
        if self.cfg.order \>= 2:
            J, Q \= self.cfg.J, self.cfg.Q
            wavelets \= self.fb.wavelets
            for idx1, (j1, q1) in enumerate(
                (j, q) for j in range(J) for q in range(Q)
            ):
                for idx2, (j2, q2) in enumerate(
                    (j, q) for j in range(J) for q in range(Q)
                ):
                    if j2 <= j1:
                        continue  \# Mallat pruning: keep only j2 > j1
                    \_, \_, psi2\_hat \= wavelets\[idx2\]
                    u1\_hat \= np.fft.fft(u1\_list\[idx1\])
                    u2 \= np.abs(self.\_convolve(u1\_hat, psi2\_hat))
                    coeffs.append(self.\_low\_pass(u2))

        out \= np.array(coeffs, dtype\=np.float32)
        \# Log compression: improves dynamic range for Laplacian distances
        return np.log1p(out)

## `scripts/scattering_integration_example.py`

This mirrors `extract_encodec_features()` in `audio_codec.py` exactly, so it drops straight into `WireGraph.build(features=...)` with no other changes.

"""Drop-in replacement for extract\_encodec\_features using wavelet scattering.
Wiring point — matches the signature of extract\_encodec\_features() in
audio\_codec.py so it can be substituted directly in build\_prior.py:
    # Before
    A = extract\_encodec\_features(loader, encoder)  # (N, 128)
    graph = WireGraph.build(features=A)
    # After
    A = extract\_scattering\_features(loader, cfg=ScatteringConfig(J=6, Q=8))
    graph = WireGraph.build(features=A)            # same API, different F
"""
from \_\_future\_\_ import annotations

import torch
from torch import Tensor

from ald\_sc.scattering1d import Scattering1D, ScatteringConfig

def extract\_scattering\_features(
    loader: torch.utils.data.DataLoader,
    cfg: ScatteringConfig | None \= None,
    signal\_length: int \= 24000,
) \-> Tensor:
    """Extract scattering features from a dataloader for prior building.
    Mirrors extract\_encodec\_features() — iterates the dataloader, computes
    a flat scattering vector per clip, and stacks into an (N, D) matrix
    suitable for WireGraph.build(features=...).
    Parameters
    ----------
    loader : DataLoader
        Yields (B, 1, T) mono waveforms (or (B, T) will be squeezed).
    cfg : ScatteringConfig, optional
        Scattering hyperparameters. Default: J=5, Q=4, order=2 → D=211.
    signal\_length : int
        Fixed signal length in samples. Clips are truncated or zero-padded.
        Default 24000 (1 second at 24 kHz, matching EnCodec's sample rate).
    Returns
    -------
    Tensor (N, D)
        Corpus scattering embeddings on CPU.
    Notes
    -----
    This is pure NumPy — no GPU path. For large corpora (>10k clips) consider
    batching the FFTs or switching to a compiled engine (kymatio, torch-scattering).
    A corpus of 2000 clips at 24 kHz with J=5, Q=4 takes ~30 s on a modern CPU.
    """
    if cfg is None:
        cfg \= ScatteringConfig(J\=5, Q\=4, order\=2)
    sc \= Scattering1D(N\=signal\_length, cfg\=cfg)
    features: list\[Tensor\] \= \[\]

    for batch in loader:
        x \= batch if isinstance(batch, Tensor) else batch\[0\]
        \# Ensure shape (B, T)
        if x.dim() \== 3:
            x \= x.squeeze(1)  \# (B, 1, T) → (B, T)
        x\_np \= x.detach().cpu().numpy().astype("float64")

        batch\_feats \= \[\]
        for clip in x\_np:
            \# Truncate or zero-pad to signal\_length
            if len(clip) \>= signal\_length:
                clip \= clip\[:signal\_length\]
            else:
                clip \= np.pad(clip, (0, signal\_length \- len(clip)))
            batch\_feats.append(sc.transform(clip))  \# (D,)

        features.append(torch.from\_numpy(np.stack(batch\_feats)))  \# (B, D)

    return torch.cat(features, dim\=0)  \# (N, D)

## Wiring into `build_prior.py`

The only change required is in the feature extraction call. `WireGraph.build()` is agnostic to feature dimension, so `L_F` will be `(D, D)` instead of `(128, 128)`, which is fine — ArrowSpace and the fallback k-NN Laplacian both accept arbitrary `(N, F)` input.

\# build\_prior.py — minimal change
from ald\_sc.scattering\_integration\_example import extract\_scattering\_features
from ald\_sc.scattering1d import ScatteringConfig

\# Option A: pure scattering
A \= extract\_scattering\_features(
    loader,
    cfg\=ScatteringConfig(J\=6, Q\=8, order\=2),  \# D=... depends on J, Q
    signal\_length\=24000,
)

\# Option B: concatenate with EnCodec pooled features
A\_enc \= extract\_encodec\_features(loader, encoder)   \# (N, 128)
A\_scat \= extract\_scattering\_features(loader)         \# (N, 211)
A \= torch.cat(\[A\_enc, A\_scat\], dim\=1)               \# (N, 339)

graph \= WireGraph.build(features\=A, k\=4)

## Hyperparameter sweep recommendation

Before trusting the resulting `L_F` geometry for LSD's corpus, sweep `J` and `Q` against ESC-50 / AudioFolder data. The key observable is intra-cluster compactness in the spectral embedding:

for J in \[4, 5, 6\]:
    for Q in \[4, 8, 12\]:
        cfg \= ScatteringConfig(J\=J, Q\=Q, order\=2)
        A \= extract\_scattering\_features(loader, cfg\=cfg)
        g \= WireGraph.build(features\=A)
        emb \= g.spectral\_embedding(n\_components\=4)  \# (N, 4)
        \# Measure cluster separation: lower intra/inter ratio is better
        print(f"J={J}, Q={Q}, D={Scattering1D(24000, cfg).feature\_dim}, nnz={g.nnz}")

**Expected baseline** (J=5, Q=4): `D=211`, scattering sensitivity ~170× lower than raw signal.

175:         m.update(arm=name, gate="USEFUL" if gate else "-")
176:         rows.append(m)
177:         print(
178:             f"[{name:>14}] L1 {m['l1_mean']:.4f} ({m['l1_min']:.4f}-"
179:             f"{m['l1_max']:.4f})  spread {m['centroid_spread_hz']:6.1f}Hz"
180:             f"  FAD {m['FAD']:7.1f}  RMS {m['RMS']:.3f}"
181:             f"  {'USEFUL' if gate else '-'}"
182:         )
183: 
184:     # Controls
185:     report("base_ddim", [_decode(dec, prior, d).cpu() for d in draws])
186:     for temp in (0.5, 1.5):
187:         report(f"temp{temp}", [_decode(dec, prior, d * temp).cpu() for d in draws])
188: 
189:     # Jitter bank

210:             [
211:                 _decode(dec, prior, (1 - alpha) * z_bar + alpha * z_anchor[i]).cpu()
212:                 for i in range(N_BANK)
213:             ],
214:         )

216:     # Stop-time variation

1: """Evaluation pipeline for the Spectral Composition paper (issue #49).
2: 
3: Owns all paper-table computations:
4: 
5: - Phase 1: train/val/test L1 reconstruction + lambda_ED ablation
6:   (``reconstruction_table``, ``ablation_table``) and per-band spectral
7:   energy retention (``band_energy_retention``, paper §6.2).
8: - Phase 2: FAD-proxy (Frechet distance over frozen EnCodec feature
9:   distributions) + CLAP-proxy (cosine on a deterministic text/audio
10:   embedding) + baseline comparison (``frechet_distance``, ``fad_score``,
11:   ``text_embedding``, ``audio_embedding``, ``clap_proxy_score``).
12: - Phase 3a: dehydration compression ratio vs corpus size N
13:   (``compression_ratio``, ``compression_ratio_vs_n``).
14: - Phase 3b: rehydration coherence (MIDI pitch contour vs spectral
15:   centroid, Pearson r) (``rehydration_coherence``) and spectral rolloff
16:   (``spectral_rolloff``, paper §6.1 rolloff drift).
17: - Phase 3c: recursive variant diversity (pairwise CLAP-proxy cosine
18:   distance vs depth) (``variant_diversity``) and TRUE R-round recursion
19:   through ``condition_on_audio`` → ``synthesize_midi``
20:   (``recursive_variant_drift``, paper §6.1 Stage 4).
21: - Phase 4: heat-death epsilon sweep (``eps_sweep``, sampling-only).
22: 
23: Dependency note. ``fadtk`` and ``laion-clap`` were removed from the project
24: due to dependency conflicts (see README "Open issues"). To stay green, the
25: Phase 2 / 3c "FAD" and "CLAP score" columns are implemented as faithful,
26: dependency-free proxies on the *same* frozen EnCodec feature space the model
27: already uses. The methodology is documented alongside each table so the
28: proxy columns are never mistaken for the original VGGish / LAION metrics.
29: 
30: This module must not define model architectures or training loops (per
31: AGENTS.md S11); it only evaluates already-trained components.
32: """
33: 
34: from __future__ import annotations
35: 
36: import hashlib
37: from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence
38: from pathlib import Path
39: 
40: import numpy as np
41: import torch
42: from torch import Tensor, nn
43: 
44: from ald_sc.arrow_prior import ArrowSpacePrior
45: from ald_sc.audio_codec import BaselineAudioDecoder, EnCodecEncoder
46: from ald_sc.losses import ALDSCLoss
47: 
48: __all__ = [
49:     "split_files",
50:     "evaluate_reconstruction",
51:     "reconstruction_table",
52:     "ablation_table",
53:     "band_energy_retention",
54:     "frechet_distance",
55:     "encodec_pooled_features",
56:     "fad_score",
57:     "text_embedding",
58:     "audio_embedding",
59:     "clap_proxy_score",
60:     "perceptual_table",
61:     "compression_ratio",
62:     "compression_ratio_vs_n",
63:     "spectral_centroid",
64:     "spectral_rolloff",
65:     "midi_pitch_contour",
66:     "rehydration_coherence",
67:     "variant_diversity",
68:     "recursive_variant_drift",
69:     "eps_sweep",
70: ]
71: 
72: SAMPLE_RATE = 24000
73: 
74: 
75: def split_files(
76:     files: Sequence[str | Path],
77:     train_frac: float = 0.7,
78:     val_frac: float = 0.15,
79:     seed: int = 3407,
80: ) -> tuple[list[Path], list[Path], list[Path]]:
81:     """Reproducible train/val/test split of a file list (mirrors nb06).
82: 
83:     The remainder after ``train_frac + val_frac`` goes to test. The split is
84:     seeded and the input list is sorted before shuffling so it is deterministic
85:     across runs and independent of the OS file order.
86:     """
87:     import random
88: 
89:     ordered = sorted(Path(f) for f in files)
90:     rng = random.Random(seed)
91:     shuffled = ordered[:]
92:     rng.shuffle(shuffled)
93:     n = len(shuffled)
94:     n_train = int(n * train_frac)
95:     n_val = int(n * val_frac)
96:     train = shuffled[:n_train]
97:     val = shuffled[n_train : n_train + n_val]
98:     test = shuffled[n_train + n_val :]
99:     return train, val, test
100: 
101: 
102: @torch.no_grad()
103: def evaluate_reconstruction(
104:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
105:     decoder: nn.Module,
106:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
107:     loader,
108:     loss_fn: ALDSCLoss,
109:     device: torch.device,
110:     use_cspec: bool = True,
111: ) -> dict[str, float]:
112:     """Mean reconstruction metrics of a decoder over a loader.
113: 
114:     Handles both graph decoders (which take ``(z, c_spec)``) and the matched
115:     baseline (which takes ``z`` only). When ``use_cspec`` is False the graph
116:     decoder receives a zeroed ``c_spec`` — the lambda_ED ablation.
117:     """
118:     encoder = encoder.to(device).eval()
119:     decoder = decoder.to(device).eval()
120:     prior = prior.to(device)
121:     is_baseline = isinstance(decoder, BaselineAudioDecoder)
122: 
123:     totals = {"rec": 0.0, "stft": 0.0, "chart": 0.0, "smooth": 0.0}
124:     n = 0
125:     for batch in loader:
126:         x = batch.to(device) if isinstance(batch, Tensor) else batch[0].to(device)
127:         z, A, c_spec = encoder.encode(x, prior)
128:         if is_baseline:
129:             x_hat = decoder(z)
130:         elif use_cspec:
131:             x_hat = decoder(z, c_spec)
132:         else:
133:             x_hat = decoder(z, torch.zeros_like(c_spec))
134:         losses = loss_fn(x, x_hat, A, A.detach())
135:         totals["rec"] += float(losses["rec"].item())
136:         totals["stft"] += float(losses["stft"].item())
137:         totals["chart"] += float(losses["chart"].item())
138:         totals["smooth"] += float(losses["smooth"].item())
139:         n += 1
140:     return {k: v / max(n, 1) for k, v in totals.items()}
141: 
142: 
143: def reconstruction_table(
144:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
145:     graph_decoder: nn.Module,
146:     baseline_decoder: nn.Module,
147:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
148:     loss_fn: ALDSCLoss,
149:     loaders: dict[str, object],
150:     device: torch.device,
151: ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
152:     """Phase 1, Table 1: mean L1 reconstruction per split per decoder.
153: 
154:     Returns one row per (split, decoder) with columns
155:     ``split, decoder, L1, stft, chart, smooth``.
156:     """
157:     rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
158:     for split_name, loader in loaders.items():
159:         for dec_name, dec in (("graph", graph_decoder), ("baseline", baseline_decoder)):
160:             m = evaluate_reconstruction(encoder, dec, prior, loader, loss_fn, device)
161:             rows.append(
162:                 {
163:                     "split": split_name,
164:                     "decoder": dec_name,
165:                     "L1": m["rec"],
166:                     "stft": m["stft"],
167:                     "chart": m["chart"],
168:                     "smooth": m["smooth"],
169:                 }
170:             )
171:     return rows
172: 
173: 
174: def ablation_table(
175:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
176:     graph_decoder: nn.Module,
177:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
178:     loss_fn: ALDSCLoss,
179:     loaders: dict[str, object],
180:     device: torch.device,
181: ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
182:     """Phase 1, Table 2: lambda_ED ablation (c_spec on vs off).
183: 
184:     For each split reports the graph-decoder L1 with and without c_spec
185:     gating, plus the lambda_ED delta (without - with; negative means gating
186:     helps reconstruction). Columns: ``split, with_cspec, L1`` and a final
187:     delta row per split.
188:     """
189:     rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
190:     for split_name, loader in loaders.items():
191:         with_c = evaluate_reconstruction(
192:             encoder, graph_decoder, prior, loader, loss_fn, device, use_cspec=True
193:         )
194:         without = evaluate_reconstruction(
195:             encoder, graph_decoder, prior, loader, loss_fn, device, use_cspec=False
196:         )
197:         rows.append({"split": split_name, "with_cspec": True, "L1": with_c["rec"]})
198:         rows.append({"split": split_name, "with_cspec": False, "L1": without["rec"]})
199:         rows.append(
200:             {
201:                 "split": split_name,
202:                 "with_cspec": "delta",
203:                 "L1": without["rec"] - with_c["rec"],
204:             }
205:         )
206:     return rows
207: 
208: 
209: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
210: # Phase 1 extension: per-band spectral energy retention (paper §6.2)
211: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
212: 
213: 
214: @torch.no_grad()
215: def band_energy_retention(
216:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
217:     decoder: nn.Module,
218:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
219:     loader,
220:     device: torch.device,
221:     use_cspec: bool = True,
222: ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
223:     """Per-mode band-energy retention of reconstructions (paper §6.2).
224: 
225:     For each batch: encode the original audio to ``A`` (pooled EnCodec
226:     features), decode to ``x_hat``, re-encode ``x_hat`` to ``A_hat``, and
227:     compare the normalised per-mode band energies ``e_tilde`` via
228:     ``prior.band_energies``. Retention per mode k is
229:     ``e_tilde_rec[k] / e_tilde_orig[k]`` (1.0 = perfect retention; guarded
230:     to 0 when the original mode carries negligible energy).
231: 
232:     Returns one row per spectral mode k with columns
233:     ``k, e_orig, e_recon, retention, cosine`` where cosine is the mean
234:     cosine similarity between the original and reconstructed band-energy
235:     vectors (repeated across rows as the split-level summary).
236:     """
237:     encoder = encoder.to(device).eval()
238:     decoder = decoder.to(device).eval()
239:     prior = prior.to(device)
240:     is_baseline = isinstance(decoder, BaselineAudioDecoder)
241: 
242:     e_orig_sum = torch.zeros(prior.q)
243:     e_rec_sum = torch.zeros(prior.q)
244:     cos_sum, n_batches = 0.0, 0
245:     for batch in loader:
246:         x = batch.to(device) if isinstance(batch, Tensor) else batch[0].to(device)
247:         z, A, c_spec = encoder.encode(x, prior)
248:         if is_baseline:
249:             x_hat = decoder(z)
250:         elif use_cspec:
251:             x_hat = decoder(z, c_spec)
252:         else:
253:             x_hat = decoder(z, torch.zeros_like(c_spec))
254:         _, A_hat, _ = encoder.encode(x_hat.clamp(-1, 1), prior)
255: 
256:         e_o = prior.band_energies(A)
257:         e_r = prior.band_energies(A_hat)
258:         e_o = e_o / (e_o.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-8)
259:         e_r = e_r / (e_r.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-8)
260:         e_orig_sum += e_o.mean(dim=0).cpu()
261:         e_rec_sum += e_r.mean(dim=0).cpu()
262:         cos = torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(e_o, e_r, dim=-1)
263:         cos_sum += float(cos.mean().item())
264:         n_batches += 1
265: 
266:     if n_batches == 0:
267:         return []
268:     e_orig_mean = e_orig_sum / n_batches
269:     e_rec_mean = e_rec_sum / n_batches
270:     cosine = cos_sum / n_batches
271:     rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
272:     for k in range(prior.q):
273:         retention = (
274:             float(e_rec_mean[k] / e_orig_mean[k]) if e_orig_mean[k] > 1e-6 else 0.0
275:         )
276:         rows.append(
277:             {
278:                 "k": k,
279:                 "e_orig": float(e_orig_mean[k]),
280:                 "e_recon": float(e_rec_mean[k]),
281:                 "retention": retention,
282:                 "cosine": cosine,
283:             }
284:         )
285:     return rows
286: 
287: 
288: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
289: # Phase 2: perceptual metrics (dependency-free proxies)
290: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
291: 
292: 
293: @torch.no_grad()
294: def encodec_pooled_features(
295:     audio_iter: Iterable[Tensor],
296:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
297:     device: torch.device,
298: ) -> Tensor:
299:     """Concatenate pooled EnCodec features (N, F) for an iterable of clips.
300: 
301:     ``audio_iter`` yields waveforms shaped (B, 1, T_audio) or (B, T_audio) or
302:     (1, 1, T_audio). Batched inputs produce multiple feature vectors.
303:     Returns a single (N, F) tensor where N is the total number of clips.
304:     """
305:     encoder = encoder.to(device).eval()
306:     feats: list[Tensor] = []
307:     for clip in audio_iter:
308:         x = clip.to(device)
309:         if x.dim() == 2:
310:             x = x.unsqueeze(0)
311:         if x.dim() == 3 and x.shape[1] != 1:
312:             x = x.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True)
313:         z = encoder.extract_features(x)
314:         feats.append(z.mean(dim=2).cpu())
315:     return torch.cat(feats, dim=0)
316: 
317: 
318: def frechet_distance(feats_a: Tensor, feats_b: Tensor) -> float:
319:     """Frechet distance between two feature distributions.
320: 
321:     ``||mu_a - mu_b||^2 + Tr(C_a + C_b - 2 (C_a C_b)^{1/2})`` on per-sample
322:     feature vectors. This is the Frechet Audio Distance formula evaluated on
323:     EnCodec pooled features (the FAD-proxy used here).
324:     """
325:     a = feats_a.detach().float()
326:     b = feats_b.detach().float()
327:     if a.dim() != 2 or b.dim() != 2:
328:         raise ValueError("frechet_distance expects (N, F) feature matrices")
329:     mu_a = a.mean(dim=0)
330:     mu_b = b.mean(dim=0)
331:     ca = torch.cov(a.T)
332:     cb = torch.cov(b.T)
333:     diff = (mu_a - mu_b).pow(2).sum().item()
334:     # eigenvalues of (Ca @ Cb) are real nonneg for PSD factors; sqrt-sum is
335:     # Tr(sqrt(Ca Cb)). Guard with symmetric sqrt via Ca^(1/2) Cb Ca^(1/2).
336:     eigvals_a, eigvecs_a = torch.linalg.eigh(ca)
337:     eigvals_a = eigvals_a.clamp(min=0)
338:     sqrt_ca = (eigvecs_a * eigvals_a.sqrt().unsqueeze(0)) @ eigvecs_a.T
339:     mid = sqrt_ca @ cb @ sqrt_ca
340:     mid = (mid + mid.T) / 2
341:     eigvals_mid = torch.linalg.eigvalsh(mid).clamp(min=0)
342:     trace_term = float(eigvals_mid.sqrt().sum().item())
343:     ca_reg = float(torch.trace(ca).item())
344:     cb_reg = float(torch.trace(cb).item())
345:     return float(diff + ca_reg + cb_reg - 2.0 * trace_term)
346: 
347: 
348: def fad_score(generated_features: Tensor, reference_features: Tensor) -> float:
349:     """FAD-proxy: Frechet distance between generated and reference feature sets.
350: 
351:     Lower is better (generated distribution closer to the reference corpus).
352:     Falls back to a simple ||mu|| difference when either set has < 2 samples
353:     (a covariance needs at least 2 points).
354:     """
355:     if generated_features.shape[0] < 2 or reference_features.shape[0] < 2:
356:         return float(
357:             (generated_features.mean(0) - reference_features.mean(0))
358:             .pow(2)
359:             .sum()
360:             .item()
361:         )
362:     val = frechet_distance(generated_features, reference_features)
363:     return max(val, 0.0)
364: 
365: 
366: def text_embedding(text: str, dim: int, salt: int = 0) -> Tensor:
367:     """Deterministic text -> dim embedding (CLAP-proxy text side).
368: 
369:     A hashing bag-of-characters projection that is fully determined by the
370:     string (and an optional salt). The result is L2-normalised. This is *not*
371:     a learned text encoder; it gives a stable, reproducible target vector so
372:     the cosine-alignment score is well defined and responds to the prompt.
373:     """
374:     vec = torch.zeros(dim, dtype=torch.float32)
375:     digest = hashlib.sha256(f"{salt}:{text}".encode("utf-8")).digest()
376:     # Walk the hash bytes, scattering signed contributions across dim. Iterate
377:     # the digest cyclically so the vector is dense for short strings.
378:     i = 0
379:     while vec.abs().sum().item() == 0 or i < max(8, dim):
380:         chunk = hashlib.sha256(digest + i.to_bytes(4, "little")).digest()
381:         for byte in chunk:
382:             sign = 1.0 if (byte & 1) else -1.0
383:             mag = ((byte >> 1) & 0x7F) / 127.0
384:             vec[(i + (byte >> 1)) % dim] += sign * mag
385:             i += 1
386:             if vec.abs().sum().item() > 0 and i >= max(8, dim):
387:                 break
388:         if i >= max(256, dim * 4):
389:             break
390:     norm = vec.norm()
391:     if norm > 0:
392:         vec = vec / norm
393:     return vec
394: 
395: 
396: @torch.no_grad()
397: def audio_embedding(
398:     audio: Tensor | Iterable[Tensor],
399:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
400:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior | None,
401:     device: torch.device,
402: ) -> Tensor:
403:     """CLAP-proxy audio side: pooled EnCodec features of one or many clips.
404: 
405:     Accepts a single (1, 1, T) clip or an iterable of clips and returns a
406:     single (F,) mean feature (for a single clip) or (N, F) features. Normalised
407:     to unit norm so cosine similarity is well scaled.
408:     """
409:     if isinstance(audio, Tensor):
410:         audio = [audio]
411:     feats = encodec_pooled_features(audio, encoder, device)
412:     if feats.shape[0] == 1:
413:         v = feats[0]
414:     else:
415:         v = feats.mean(dim=0)
416:     norm = v.norm()
417:     if norm > 0:
418:         v = v / norm
419:     return v
420: 
421: 
422: def clap_proxy_score(
423:     generated_audio: list[Tensor],
424:     text_prompt: str,
425:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
426:     device: torch.device,
427: ) -> float:
428:     """Mean cosine similarity between generated clips and a text prompt.
429: 
430:     Audio side = L2-normalised mean EnCodec-pooled feature of the generated
431:     bank; text side = L2-normalised deterministic hashing embedding of the
432:     prompt into the same F dimensions. Returns a scalar in [-1, 1]. This is the
433:     documented CLAP-proxy (not LAION-CLAP).
434:     """
435:     audio_vec = audio_embedding(generated_audio, encoder, None, device)
436:     feat_dim = audio_vec.shape[0]
437:     text_vec = text_embedding(text_prompt, feat_dim).to(audio_vec.device)
438:     return float(torch.cosine_similarity(audio_vec, text_vec, dim=0).item())
439: 
440: 
441: def perceptual_table(
442:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
443:     graph_decoder: nn.Module,
444:     baseline_decoder: nn.Module,
445:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
446:     dit: nn.Module,
447:     sched,
448:     reference_features: Tensor,
449:     text_prompt: str,
450:     device: torch.device,
451:     n_gen: int = 16,
452:     steps: int = 50,
453:     seed: int = 3407,
454: ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
455:     """Phase 2, Table 3: FAD-proxy + CLAP-proxy for graph vs baseline.
456: 
457:     Generates ``n_gen`` latents via DDIM, decodes with each decoder, and
458:     compares the resulting audio feature distribution to ``reference_features``
459:     (the held-out test-set EnCodec features). Also reports the CLAP-proxy
460:     alignment between the generated bank and ``text_prompt``.
461:     """
462:     from ald_sc.sampling import sample_ddim
463: 
464:     rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
465:     encoder = encoder.to(device).eval()
466:     prior = prior.to(device)
467:     dit = dit.to(device).eval()
468: 
469:     def _gen_audio(decoder, use_cspec: bool) -> list[Tensor]:
470:         clips: list[Tensor] = []
471:         for i in range(n_gen):
472:             z = sample_ddim(
473:                 dit,
474:                 sched,
475:                 batch_size=1,
476:                 steps=steps,
477:                 seed=seed + i,
478:                 device=device,
479:             )
480:             a = z.mean(dim=2)
481:             c_spec = prior.chart_energy_descriptor(a)
482:             if isinstance(decoder, BaselineAudioDecoder):
483:                 x_hat = decoder(z)
484:             elif use_cspec:
485:                 x_hat = decoder(z, c_spec)
486:             else:
487:                 x_hat = decoder(z, torch.zeros_like(c_spec))
488:             x_hat = x_hat.clamp(-1, 1).squeeze(0)
489:             peak = x_hat.abs().max()
490:             if peak > 0:
491:                 x_hat = x_hat / peak
492:             clips.append(x_hat.unsqueeze(0))
493:         return clips
494: 
495:     for name, dec, use_c in (
496:         ("graph", graph_decoder, True),
497:         ("baseline", baseline_decoder, False),
498:     ):
499:         clips = _gen_audio(dec, use_c)
500:         gen_feats = encodec_pooled_features(clips, encoder, device)
501:         # Both feature sets are on CPU (encodec_pooled_features moves to CPU).
502:         fad = fad_score(gen_feats, reference_features.cpu())
503:         clap = clap_proxy_score(clips, text_prompt, encoder, device)
504:         rows.append(
505:             {
506:                 "decoder": name,
507:                 "FAD": fad,
508:                 "FAD_method": "encod_proxy",
509:                 "CLAP": clap,
510:                 "CLAP_method": "encod_proxy",
511:             }
512:         )
513:     return rows
514: 
515: 
516: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
517: # Phase 3a: dehydration compression ratio
518: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
519: 
520: 
521: def _prior_float_count(prior: ArrowSpacePrior) -> int:
522:     """Number of float32 values stored in the dehydrated prior."""
523:     n = 0
524:     for buf_name in ("L_F", "U_q", "eigvals_q", "lambdas_ed", "lambdas_chart"):
525:         buf = getattr(prior, buf_name, None)
526:         if buf is not None:
527:             n += int(buf.numel())
528:     return n
529: 
530: 
531: def compression_ratio(
532:     n_clips: int,
533:     audio_length: int,
534:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
535:     bits_per_pcm_sample: int = 16,
536:     bits_per_latent_element: int = 16,
537:     latent_length: int | None = None,
538:     latent_channels: int = 128,
539:     encod_bandwidth_kbps: int = 24,
540:     use_code_rate: bool = True,
541: ) -> dict[str, float]:
542:     """Dehydration compression ratio for a corpus of ``n_clips``.
543: 
544:     Two representations are compared:
545: 
546:     - **Raw audio**: ``n_clips * audio_length * bits_per_pcm_sample`` bits
547:       (16-bit PCM library).
548:     - **Dehydrated**: the shared ArrowSpace prior
549:       ``(L_F, U_q, eigvals_q, lambda_ED, lambda_chart)`` stored once (in
550:       float32 = 32 bits/value) plus per-clip latent storage. The latent
551:       storage models EnCodec's actual compressed rate:
552:       ``encod_bandwidth_kbps * (audio_length / sample_rate)`` bits/clip. Set
553:       ``use_code_rate=False`` to instead count latent tensors as
554:       ``latent_channels * latent_length * bits_per_latent_element``.
555: 
556:     Returns raw/dehydrated bit counts and the ratio raw/dehydrated. The
557:     prior is constant across N, so the ratio grows with N and asymptotes to
558:     the per-clip code rate ratio (the prior amortises).
559:     """
560:     raw_bits = float(n_clips * audio_length * bits_per_pcm_sample)
561:     prior_bits = float(_prior_float_count(prior) * 32)
562:     if use_code_rate:
563:         latent_bits_per_clip = float(
564:             encod_bandwidth_kbps * 1000 * (audio_length / SAMPLE_RATE)
565:         )
566:     else:
567:         if latent_length is None:
568:             latent_length = audio_length // 320
569:         latent_bits_per_clip = float(
570:             latent_channels * latent_length * bits_per_latent_element
571:         )
572:     dehydrated_bits = prior_bits + n_clips * latent_bits_per_clip
573:     ratio = raw_bits / dehydrated_bits if dehydrated_bits > 0 else float("inf")
574:     return {
575:         "N": n_clips,
576:         "raw_bits": raw_bits,
577:         "prior_bits": prior_bits,
578:         "latent_bits_per_clip": latent_bits_per_clip,
579:         "dehydrated_bits": dehydrated_bits,
580:         "compression_ratio": ratio,
581:     }
582: 
583: 
584: def compression_ratio_vs_n(
585:     n_values: Sequence[int],
586:     audio_length: int,
587:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
588:     **kwargs,
589: ) -> list[dict[str, float]]:
590:     """Compression ratio as a function of corpus size N (Table 4 rows)."""
591:     return [compression_ratio(n, audio_length, prior, **kwargs) for n in n_values]
592:

594: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
595: # Phase 3b: rehydration coherence
596: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
597: 
598: 
599: def spectral_centroid(
600:     audio: Tensor, sample_rate: int = SAMPLE_RATE, n_fft: int = 2048, hop: int = 512
601: ) -> Tensor:
602:     """Per-frame spectral centroid (1-D tensor) of a mono waveform.
603: 
604:     centroid(t) = sum_f f * |X(t,f)| / sum_f |X(t,f)|.
605: 
606:     Accepts (T,) or (1, T) or (1, 1, T). Returns (num_frames,) centroid in Hz.
607:     """
608:     x = audio.detach().float().cpu()
609:     if x.dim() == 3:
610:         x = x.squeeze(0).squeeze(0)
611:     elif x.dim() == 2:
612:         x = x.squeeze(0)
613:     window = torch.hann_window(n_fft)
614:     spec = torch.stft(
615:         x,
616:         n_fft,
617:         hop_length=hop,
618:         return_complex=True,
619:         window=window,
620:     )
621:     mag = spec.abs().clamp(min=1e-12)
622:     freqs = torch.linspace(0, sample_rate / 2, mag.shape[0])
623:     centroid = (freqs[:, None] * mag).sum(dim=0) / mag.sum(dim=0)
624:     return centroid
625: 
626: 
627: def spectral_rolloff(
628:     audio: Tensor,
629:     sample_rate: int = SAMPLE_RATE,
630:     n_fft: int = 2048,
631:     hop: int = 512,
632:     fraction: float = 0.85,
633: ) -> Tensor:
634:     """Per-frame spectral rolloff (1-D tensor) of a mono waveform.
635: 
636:     rolloff(t) = the lowest frequency f such that ``fraction`` of the
637:     frame's spectral energy is contained in bins <= f (classic 0.85
638:     rolloff). Accepts (T,), (1, T) or (1, 1, T). Returns (num_frames,)
639:     rolloff frequencies in Hz.
640:     """
641:     x = audio.detach().float().cpu()
642:     if x.dim() == 3:
643:         x = x.squeeze(0).squeeze(0)
644:     elif x.dim() == 2:
645:         x = x.squeeze(0)
646:     window = torch.hann_window(n_fft)
647:     spec = torch.stft(
648:         x,
649:         n_fft,
650:         hop_length=hop,
651:         return_complex=True,
652:         window=window,
653:     )
654:     mag = spec.abs().clamp(min=0.0)
655:     freqs = torch.linspace(0, sample_rate / 2, mag.shape[0])
656:     energy = mag.pow(2)
657:     cum = torch.cumsum(energy, dim=0)
658:     total = cum[-1:, :]
659:     crossed = cum >= fraction * total
660:     # First bin where the cumulative energy crosses the fraction threshold.
661:     idx = crossed.float().argmax(dim=0)
662:     return freqs[idx]
663: 
664: 
665: def midi_pitch_contour(
666:     events: Sequence[tuple[int, float, float]],
667:     num_frames: int,
668:     sample_rate: int = SAMPLE_RATE,
669:     hop: int = 512,
670: ) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
671:     """Sample the MIDI pitch contour (semitones) at the centroid frame times.
672: 
673:     Returns ``(contour, mask)`` of length ``num_frames``. ``mask`` is True on
674:     frames where a note is active; ``contour`` is the MIDI note number on
675:     active frames and 0 elsewhere.
676:     """
677:     times = torch.arange(num_frames) * hop / sample_rate
678:     contour = torch.zeros(num_frames)
679:     mask = torch.zeros(num_frames, dtype=torch.bool)
680:     for note, start, dur in sorted(events, key=lambda e: e[1]):
681:         lo = start
682:         hi = start + dur
683:         active = (times >= lo) & (times < hi)
684:         contour[active] = float(note)
685:         mask[active] = True
686:     return contour, mask
687: 
688: 
689: def rehydration_coherence(
690:     model,
691:     events: Sequence[tuple[int, float, float]],
692:     bank,
693:     pitch_bank_root: int = 60,
694: ) -> dict[str, object]:
695:     """Phase 3b: coherence of a rehydrated render vs its MIDI score.
696: 
697:     Renders ``events`` with ``model.synthesize_midi`` (Mode C), computes the
698:     spectral-centroid contour of the render, the MIDI pitch contour sampled at
699:     the same frames, and reports the Pearson correlation between the two over
700:     frames where a note is active. A higher r means the rehydrated audio's
701:     spectral centroid tracks the scored pitch contour.
702:     """
703:     audio = model.synthesize_midi(
704:         list(events), list(bank), pitch_bank_root=pitch_bank_root, seed=3407
705:     )
706:     sr = model.sample_rate
707:     centroid = spectral_centroid(audio, sample_rate=sr)
708:     num_frames = centroid.shape[0]
709:     contour, mask = midi_pitch_contour(events, num_frames, sample_rate=sr)
710:     if mask.sum() >= 2:
711:         a = contour[mask].numpy().astype(np.float64)
712:         b = centroid[mask].numpy().astype(np.float64)
713:         if a.std() > 0 and b.std() > 0:
714:             r = float(np.corrcoef(a, b)[0, 1])
715:         else:
716:             r = 0.0
717:     else:
718:         r = float("nan")
719:     n_notes = int(mask.sum().item())
720:     return {
721:         "midi_events": len(events),
722:         "active_frames": n_notes,
723:         "pearson_r": r,
724:         "centroid_mean_hz": float(centroid.mean().item()),
725:         "centroid_std_hz": float(centroid.std().item()),
726:     }
727: 
728: 
729: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
730: # Phase 3c: recursive variant diversity
731: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
732: 
733: 
734: def variant_diversity(
735:     make_variants,
736:     depths: Sequence[int],
737:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
738:     device: torch.device,
739: ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
740:     """Mean pairwise CLAP-proxy cosine *distance* vs recursion depth.
741: 
742:     ``make_variants(d)`` must return a list of ``d`` audio clips (one per
743:     distinct MIDI at "depth" d). The function embeds them via the FAD-proxy
744:     audio embedding and reports the mean pairwise cosine distance
745:     (1 - cosine) among them; depth 1 trivially yields 0.0 (a single variant
746:     has no inter-variant distance).
747: 
748:     Returns one row per depth: ``depth, n_variants, mean_distance,
749:     min_distance, max_distance``.
750:     """
751:     rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
752:     for d in depths:
753:         clips = list(make_variants(d))
754:         if d <= 1 or len(clips) < 2:
755:             rows.append(
756:                 {
757:                     "depth": d,
758:                     "n_variants": len(clips),
759:                     "mean_distance": 0.0,
760:                     "min_distance": 0.0,
761:                     "max_distance": 0.0,
762:                 }
763:             )
764:             continue
765:         feats = encodec_pooled_features(clips, encoder, device)
766:         feats = feats.to(device)
767:         norms = feats.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp(min=1e-12)
768:         unit = feats / norms
769:         sim = unit @ unit.T
770:         dist = 1.0 - sim
771:         iu = torch.triu_indices(d, d, offset=1)
772:         pairs = dist[iu[0], iu[1]]
773:         rows.append(
774:             {
775:                 "depth": d,
776:                 "n_variants": d,
777:                 "mean_distance": float(pairs.mean().item()),
778:                 "min_distance": float(pairs.min().item()),
779:                 "max_distance": float(pairs.max().item()),
780:             }
781:         )
782:     return rows
783: 
784: 
785: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
786: # Phase 3c extension: TRUE recursive variant drift (paper §6.1, Stage 4)
787: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
788: 
789: 
790: def _as_clip(audio: Tensor) -> Tensor:
791:     """Normalise a waveform to (1, 1, T); keeps its device."""
792:     x = audio.detach().float()
793:     while x.dim() < 3:
794:         x = x.unsqueeze(0)
795:     if x.shape[1] != 1:
796:         x = x.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True)
797:     return x
798: 
799: 
800: def recursive_variant_drift(
801:     model,
802:     events: Sequence[tuple[int, float, float]],
803:     rounds: int,
804:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
805:     device: torch.device,
806:     steps: int = 50,
807:     seed: int = 3407,
808:     bank_n: int = 4,
809:     strength: float = 0.5,
810: ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
811:     """True R-round recursion: feed outputs back through the workflow.
812: 
813:     Round 0 renders ``events`` from a freshly generated bank. Round r
814:     conditions on the previous round's render (``condition_on_audio``),
815:     rebuilds the bank, and re-renders the same score (``synthesize_midi``).
816:     Reports per round: spectral centroid / rolloff means (drift) and the
817:     CLAP-proxy cosine distance of the round's render to the round-0 render
818:     (cumulative novelty). This replaces the earlier MIDI-rotation
819:     approximation of "depth" with faithful recursive feeding.
820:     """
821:     bank = model.generate_sound_bank(n=bank_n, steps=steps, seed=seed)
822:     audio = _as_clip(model.synthesize_midi(list(events), list(bank), seed=seed))
823: 
824:     base_feat = encodec_pooled_features([audio], encoder, device)[0]
825:     base_feat = base_feat / base_feat.norm().clamp(min=1e-12)
826: 
827:     rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
828: 
829:     def _row(r: int, clip: Tensor) -> dict[str, object]:
830:         centroid = spectral_centroid(clip, sample_rate=model.sample_rate)
831:         rolloff = spectral_rolloff(clip, sample_rate=model.sample_rate)
832:         feat = encodec_pooled_features([clip], encoder, device)[0]
833:         feat = feat / feat.norm().clamp(min=1e-12)
834:         dist = 1.0 - float(torch.dot(feat, base_feat).item())
835:         return {
836:             "round": r,
837:             "centroid_mean_hz": float(centroid.mean().item()),
838:             "centroid_std_hz": float(centroid.std().item()),
839:             "rolloff_mean_hz": float(rolloff.mean().item()),
840:             "clap_distance_to_round0": max(dist, 0.0),
841:         }
842: 
843:     rows.append(_row(0, audio))
844:     for r in range(1, rounds + 1):
845:         variants = model.condition_on_audio(
846:             audio, n=bank_n, steps=steps, strength=strength, seed=seed + r
847:         )
848:         audio = _as_clip(
849:             model.synthesize_midi(list(events), list(variants), seed=seed + r)
850:         )
851:         rows.append(_row(r, audio))
852:     return rows
853:

855: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
856: # Phase 4: heat-death epsilon sweep (sampling-only)
857: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
858: 
859: 
860: @torch.no_grad()
861: def eps_sweep(
862:     dit: nn.Module,
863:     sched,
864:     prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
865:     decoder: nn.Module,
866:     encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
867:     reference_features: Tensor,
868:     eps_values: Sequence[float],
869:     device: torch.device,
870:     n_gen: int = 8,
871:     steps: int = 50,
872:     seed: int = 3407,
873: ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
874:     """Heat-death stopping sweep: steps used + FAD-proxy vs epsilon.
875: 
876:     For each epsilon a :class:`SpectralSchedule` with that heat-death
877:     threshold drives DDIM early stopping. Reports mean steps actually used,
878:     the FAD-proxy of the generated bank against ``reference_features``,
879:     and the per-generation step counts. Sampling-only: no retraining.
880:     Larger epsilon stops earlier (fewer steps, faster, potentially worse).
881: 
882:     Note: ``prior.F`` must match the DiT latent channels (128 in the real
883:     pipeline) — c_spec is derived from the pooled latent exactly as in
884:     ``perceptual_table``.
885:     """
886:     from ald_sc.sampling import sample_ddim
887:     from ald_sc.spectral_schedule import SpectralSchedule
888: 
889:     dit = dit.to(device).eval()
890:     decoder = decoder.to(device).eval()
891:     prior = prior.to(device)
892:     encoder = encoder.to(device).eval()
893: 
894:     rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
895:     for eps in eps_values:
896:         spec_sched = SpectralSchedule(prior=prior, horizon=1.0, eps=float(eps))
897:         clips: list[Tensor] = []
898:         steps_used: list[int] = []
899:         for i in range(n_gen):
900:             z, used = sample_ddim(
901:                 dit,
902:                 sched,
903:                 batch_size=1,
904:                 steps=steps,
905:                 seed=seed + i,
906:                 device=device,
907:                 spectral_schedule=spec_sched,
908:                 return_steps=True,
909:             )
910:             a = z.mean(dim=2)
911:             c_spec = prior.chart_energy_descriptor(a)
912:             if isinstance(decoder, BaselineAudioDecoder):
913:                 x_hat = decoder(z)
914:             else:
915:                 x_hat = decoder(z, c_spec)
916:             x_hat = x_hat.clamp(-1, 1).squeeze(0)
917:             peak = x_hat.abs().max()
918:             if peak > 0:
919:                 x_hat = x_hat / peak
920:             clips.append(x_hat.unsqueeze(0))
921:             steps_used.append(int(used))
922:         gen_feats = encodec_pooled_features(clips, encoder, device)
923:         fad = fad_score(gen_feats, reference_features.cpu())
924:         rows.append(
925:             {
926:                 "eps": float(eps),
927:                 "mean_steps": sum(steps_used) / len(steps_used),
928:                 "min_steps": min(steps_used),
929:                 "max_steps": max(steps_used),
930:                 "FAD": fad,
931:                 "FAD_method": "encod_proxy",
932:                 "n_gen": n_gen,
933:             }
934:         )
935:     return rows

72: def _normalize(audio: Tensor) -> Tensor:

74:     peak = audio.abs().max()
75:     if peak > 0:
76:         return audio / peak
77:     return audio

80: class LSDModel:
81:     """Inference-time bundle of a trained LSD model.
82: 
83:     Parameters
84:     ----------
85:     prior : ArrowSpacePrior
86:         Frozen ArrowSpace prior (provides the spectral chart).
87:     dit : nn.Module
88:         Trained 1-D DiT denoiser (``latent_shape`` attribute required).
89:     decoder : nn.Module
90:         Trained graph or baseline audio decoder.
91:     encoder : EnCodecEncoder or compatible
92:         Frozen encoder used for audio-conditioned variants (mode B).
93:         Must expose ``encode(x, prior) -> (z, A, c_spec)``.
94:     schedule : CosineSchedule
95:         Noise schedule for DDIM sampling.
96:     sample_rate : int
97:         Output sample rate (default 24000 for EnCodec 24kHz).
98:     """
99: 
100:     def __init__(
101:         self,
102:         prior: ArrowSpacePrior,
103:         dit: nn.Module,
104:         decoder: nn.Module,
105:         encoder: EnCodecEncoder,
106:         schedule: CosineSchedule,
107:         sample_rate: int = 24000,
108:     ) -> None:
109:         self.prior = prior
110:         self.dit = dit
111:         self.decoder = decoder
112:         self.encoder = encoder
113:         self.schedule = schedule
114:         self.sample_rate = sample_rate
115:         self._is_baseline = isinstance(decoder, BaselineAudioDecoder)
116: 
117:     def store(
118:         self,
119:         root_dir: str | Path,
120:         slug: str = "lsd-model",
121:         hyperparams: dict | None = None,
122:     ) -> Path:
123:         """Save model artefacts and a metadata.json for reproducibility.
124: 
125:         Creates <root_dir>/<timestamp>-<slug>/ (timestamp = YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS)
126:         and writes prior.pt, decoder.pt, dit.pt, and metadata.json (sample
127:         rate, latent shape, decoder type, schedule steps, hyperparams).
128:         Returns the model directory path.
129:         """
130:         root_dir = Path(root_dir)
131:         ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
132:         safe_slug = (
133:             "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_" else "-" for c in slug) or "model"
134:         )
135:         model_dir = root_dir / f"{ts}-{safe_slug}"
136:         model_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
137: 
138:         torch.save(self.prior, model_dir / "prior.pt")
139:         torch.save(self.decoder.state_dict(), model_dir / "decoder.pt")
140:         torch.save(self.dit.state_dict(), model_dir / "dit.pt")
141: 
142:         latent_channels, latent_length = getattr(self.dit, "latent_shape", (None, None))
143:         schedule_steps = getattr(self.schedule, "num_steps", None)
144:         metadata = {
145:             "created_at": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
146:             "sample_rate": self.sample_rate,
147:             "latent_channels": latent_channels,
148:             "latent_length": latent_length,
149:             "decoder_type": type(self.decoder).__module__
150:             + "."
151:             + type(self.decoder).__name__,
152:             "schedule_num_steps": schedule_steps,
153:             "hyperparameters": dict(hyperparams) if hyperparams else {},
154:         }
155:         (model_dir / "metadata.json").write_text(json.dumps(metadata, indent=2))
156:         log.info(
157:             "model_store",
158:             slug=safe_slug,
159:             path=str(model_dir),
160:             hyperparameters=metadata["hyperparameters"],
161:         )
162:         return model_dir
163: 
164:     @torch.no_grad()
165:     def _sample_and_decode(
166:         self,
167:         seed: int,
168:         steps: int,
169:         temperature: float,
170:         z_init: Tensor | None = None,
171:     ) -> Tensor:
172:         """Sample (or use a provided) latent and decode it to a waveform."""
173:         device = next(self.dit.parameters()).device
174: 
175:         if z_init is None:
176:             z = sample_ddim(
177:                 self.dit,
178:                 self.schedule,
179:                 batch_size=1,
180:                 steps=steps,
181:                 seed=seed,
182:                 device=device,
183:             )
184:         else:
185:             z = z_init.to(device)
186: 
187:         z = _apply_temperature(z, temperature)
188:         a = z.mean(dim=2)
189:         c_spec = self.prior.chart_energy_descriptor(a)
190: 
191:         if self._is_baseline:
192:             audio = self.decoder(z)
193:         else:
194:             audio = self.decoder(z, c_spec)
195:         # Decoder returns (B, 1, T); collapse the mono channel to (1, T).
196:         audio = audio.squeeze(1)
197:         return _normalize(audio.clamp(-1, 1))
198: 
199:     @torch.no_grad()
200:     def generate_sound_bank(
201:         self,
202:         n: int = 8,
203:         steps: int = 50,
204:         temperature: float = 1.0,
205:         seed: int | None = None,
206:     ) -> list[Tensor]:
207:         """Mode A: generate a bank of ``n`` unconditional baseline sounds.
208: 
209:         Parameters
210:         ----------
211:         n : int
212:             Number of sounds to generate.
213:         steps : int
214:             DDIM sampling steps.
215:         temperature : float
216:             Noise scaling (lower = more conservative).
217:         seed : int or None
218:             Reproducible seed, or ``None`` for a non-repeatable run.
219: 
220:         Returns
221:         -------
222:         list[Tensor]
223:             ``n`` peak-normalised waveforms of shape ``(1, T)``.
224:         """
225:         s = _resolve_seed(seed)
226:         bank: list[Tensor] = []
227:         for i in range(n):
228:             clip = self._sample_and_decode(
229:                 seed=s + i, steps=steps, temperature=temperature
230:             )
231:             bank.append(clip)
232:         log.info("sound_bank", n=n, steps=steps, temperature=temperature, seed=s)
233:         return bank
234: 
235:     @torch.no_grad()
236:     def condition_on_audio(
237:         self,
238:         audio: Tensor,
239:         n: int = 4,
240:         steps: int = 50,
241:         strength: float = 0.5,
242:         temperature: float = 1.0,
243:         seed: int | None = None,
244:     ) -> list[Tensor]:
245:         """Mode B: generate ``n`` novelty variants of a producer sound.
246: 
247:         The conditioning audio is encoded to its EnCodec latent; each
248:         variant is produced by interpolating from that latent toward a
249:         fresh noise draw (``strength`` controls how far from the source),
250:         then decoding with the graph decoder.
251: 
252:         Parameters
253:         ----------
254:         audio : Tensor (1, 1, T_audio) or (1, T_audio)
255:             The conditioning sound (must be encodable by ``self.encoder``).
256:         n : int
257:             Number of variants.
258:         steps : int
259:             DDIM sampling steps.
260:         strength : float
261:             0 < strength <= 1. Larger values push further from the source
262:             (more novelty); smaller values stay closer.
263:         temperature : float
264:             Noise scaling applied after interpolation.
265:         seed : int or None
266:             Reproducible seed, or ``None`` for a non-repeatable run.
267: 
268:         Returns
269:         -------
270:         list[Tensor]
271:             ``n`` peak-normalised variant waveforms of shape ``(1, T)``.
272:         """
273:         if audio.dim() == 2:
274:             audio = audio.unsqueeze(0)
275:         if audio.dim() != 3 or audio.shape[1] != 1:
276:             raise ValueError(
277:                 f"audio must be (1, 1, T) or (1, T); got {tuple(audio.shape)}"
278:             )
279:         # Conditioning audio may arrive on CPU (e.g. bank clips staged on CPU
280:         # before MPS rendering) — move it to the model's device before encoding.
281:         audio = audio.to(self.prior.U_q.device)
282: 
283:         strength = float(max(0.0, min(1.0, strength)))
284:         s = _resolve_seed(seed)
285: 
286:         z_cond, _, _ = self.encoder.encode(audio, self.prior)
287: 
288:         variants: list[Tensor] = []
289:         for i in range(n):
290:             noise = torch.randn_like(
291:                 z_cond,
292:                 generator=torch.Generator(device=z_cond.device).manual_seed(s + i),
293:             )
294:             z = (1.0 - strength) * z_cond + strength * noise
295:             clip = self._sample_and_decode(
296:                 seed=s + i, steps=steps, temperature=temperature, z_init=z
297:             )
298:             variants.append(clip)
299:         log.info(
300:             "condition_variants",
301:             n=n,
302:             steps=steps,
303:             strength=strength,
304:             seed=s,
305:         )
306:         return variants
307: 
308:     @torch.no_grad()
309:     def synthesize_midi(
310:         self,
311:         events: list[MidiEvent],
312:         bank: list[Tensor],
313:         pitch_bank_root: int = 60,
314:         seed: int | None = None,
315:     ) -> Tensor:
316:         """Mode C: render a MIDI note sequence using generated bank sounds.
317: 
318:         Each MIDI note selects a bank sound (round-robin over ``bank``),
319:         pitch-shifts it from ``pitch_bank_root`` to the requested note via
320:         resampling, time-scales it to the requested duration, and places it
321:         at the requested start time in a mono output buffer.
322: 
323:         Parameters
324:         ----------
325:         events : list of (midi_note, start_seconds, duration_seconds)
326:             The MIDI sequence.
327:         bank : list[Tensor]
328:             Output sounds (e.g. from ``generate_sound_bank``). Must be
329:             non-empty; each element is ``(1, T)``.
330:         pitch_bank_root : int
331:             MIDI note that the bank sounds are assumed to be centred on
332:             (used as the pitch-shift reference).
333:         seed : int or None
334:             Seed for round-robin / jitter; ``None`` for non-repeatable.
335: 
336:         Returns
337:         -------
338:         Tensor (1, T_out)
339:             Mono render covering all events.
340:         """
341:         if not bank:
342:             raise ValueError("synthesize_midi requires a non-empty bank")
343: 
344:         sr = self.sample_rate
345:         events = sorted(events, key=lambda e: e[1])
346: 
347:         total_seconds = 0.0
348:         for _, start, dur in events:
349:             total_seconds = max(total_seconds, start + dur)
350:         total_seconds = max(total_seconds, 0.1)
351:         out = torch.zeros(1, int(total_seconds * sr) + 1, device=bank[0].device)
352: 
353:         s = _resolve_seed(seed)
354: 
355:         for i, (note, start, dur) in enumerate(events):
356:             src = bank[i % len(bank)].squeeze(0)  # (T,)
357:             # Pitch shift via resample ratio (semitones from pitch_bank_root).
358:             semitones = note - pitch_bank_root
359:             ratio = 2.0 ** (-semitones / 12.0)
360:             new_len = max(1, int(src.shape[-1] * ratio))
361: 
362:             pitched = _resample_1d(src, new_len)
363: 
364:             # Time-scale to requested duration.
365:             target_len = max(1, int(dur * sr))
366:             if pitched.shape[-1] != target_len:
367:                 pitched = _resample_1d(pitched, target_len)
368: 
369:             offset = int(start * sr)
370:             end = min(out.shape[-1], offset + pitched.shape[-1])
371:             out[0, offset:end] += pitched[: end - offset]
372: 
373:         log.info(
374:             "midi_render",
375:             n_events=len(events),
376:             bank_size=len(bank),
377:             pitch_bank_root=pitch_bank_root,
378:             seed=s,
379:         )
380:         return _normalize(out)

415:         timestamp, and provenance. Returns the bank directory path.

421:         clip_entries = []

423:             fname = f"{i:02d}.wav"
424:             wave = clip.squeeze(0).numpy()
425:             soundfile.write(str(bank_dir / fname), wave, self.model.sample_rate)
426:             clip_entries.append({"file": fname, "shape": list(clip.shape)})
427: 
428:         manifest = {
429:             "name": self.name,
430:             "n_clips": len(self.clips),
431:             "sample_rate": self.model.sample_rate,
432:             "generated_at": self.generated_at,
433:             "clips": clip_entries,
434:         }
435:         (bank_dir / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2))
436:         log.info(
437:             "bank_store",
438:             name=self.name,
439:             n_clips=len(self.clips),
440:             path=str(bank_dir),
441:         )
442:         return bank_dir

1: """Inference samplers for ALD-SC latent diffusion.
2: 
3: Provides Euler and DDIM-style deterministic samplers that turn noise into
4: a 1-D audio latent, which can then be decoded through the graph decoder
5: to produce a waveform.
6: 
7: When a ``SpectralSchedule`` is provided, the sampler uses the
8: Barontini-inspired heat-death stopping criterion: sampling terminates
9: when ``Σ ν_k · ᾱ_k(t) < ε``, rather than at a fixed step count.
10: 
11: This module must not add training logic (per AGENTS.md §11).
12: """
13: 
14: from __future__ import annotations
15: 
16: from collections.abc import Iterator
17: 
18: import torch
19: from torch import Tensor, nn
20: 
21: from ald_sc.schedule import CosineSchedule
22: from ald_sc.spectral_schedule import SpectralSchedule
23: 
24: __all__ = ["sample_euler", "sample_ddim", "sample_ddim_steps"]
25: 
26: 
27: def _pairwise(iterable: list[int]) -> Iterator[tuple[int, int]]:
28:     it = iter(iterable)
29:     try:
30:         prev = next(it)
31:     except StopIteration:
32:         return
33:     for curr in it:
34:         yield prev, curr
35:         prev = curr
36: 
37: 
38: def _init_noise(
39:     model: nn.Module, batch_size: int, device: torch.device, gen: torch.Generator
40: ) -> Tensor:
41:     """Initialise noise latent from the model's latent_shape attribute."""
42:     latent_channels = getattr(model, "latent_channels", 4)
43:     latent_shape = getattr(model, "latent_shape", None)
44:     if latent_shape is not None:
45:         return torch.randn(batch_size, *latent_shape, device=device, generator=gen)
46:     # Fallback for models without latent_shape
47:     latent_length = getattr(model, "latent_length", None)
48:     if latent_length is not None:
49:         return torch.randn(
50:             batch_size, latent_channels, latent_length, device=device, generator=gen
51:         )
52:     latent_size = getattr(model, "latent_size", 32)
53:     return torch.randn(
54:         batch_size,
55:         latent_channels,
56:         latent_size,
57:         latent_size,
58:         device=device,
59:         generator=gen,
60:     )
61: 
62: 
63: @torch.no_grad()
64: def sample_euler(
65:     model: nn.Module,
66:     schedule: CosineSchedule,
67:     c_spec: Tensor | None = None,
68:     batch_size: int = 1,
69:     steps: int = 50,
70:     seed: int = 3407,
71:     device: torch.device = torch.device("cpu"),
72:     spectral_schedule: SpectralSchedule | None = None,
73:     return_steps: bool = False,
74: ) -> Tensor | tuple[Tensor, int]:
75:     """Euler sampler for latent diffusion.
76: 
77:     Starts from pure noise at t=T and steps backward to t=0.
78: 
79:     Parameters
80:     ----------
81:     model : nn.Module
82:         DiT denoiser predicting velocity v.
83:     schedule : CosineSchedule
84:         Noise schedule.
85:     c_spec : Tensor (B, spec_dim), optional
86:         Spectral conditioning vector.
87:     batch_size : int
88:     steps : int
89:         Maximum number of sampling steps.
90:     seed : int
91:     device : torch.device
92:     spectral_schedule : SpectralSchedule, optional
93:         If provided, sampling stops early when the heat-death criterion
94:         remaining dissipation ``Σ ν_k · (1 − ᾱ_k(t)) < ε`` is met.
95:     return_steps : bool
96:         If True, return (z, steps_used).
97: 
98:     Returns
99:     -------
100:     Tensor
101:         Denoised latent z_0. If return_steps, returns (z, steps_used).
102:     """
103:     gen = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(seed)
104:     model = model.to(device).eval()
105:     if c_spec is not None:
106:         c_spec = c_spec.to(device)
107: 
108:     sigmas = schedule.sample_sigmas(steps).to(device)
109: 
110:     x = _init_noise(model, batch_size, device, gen)
111: 
112:     steps_used = 0
113:     for sig, sig_prev in _pairwise(sigmas.tolist()):
114:         if spectral_schedule is not None:
115:             t_frac = sig / schedule.num_steps
116:             if spectral_schedule.is_heat_death(torch.tensor(t_frac, device=device)):
117:                 break
118:         steps_used += 1
119:         t = torch.full((batch_size,), int(sig), device=device, dtype=torch.long)
120:         v = model(x, t, c_spec=c_spec)
121: 
122:         ab = schedule.alpha_bar[int(sig)]
123:         ab_prev = schedule.alpha_bar[int(sig_prev)]
124:         sqrt_ab_prev = ab_prev.sqrt()
125:         sqrt_1mab_prev = (1 - ab_prev).sqrt()
126:         sqrt_ab = ab.sqrt()
127: 
128:         z0_pred = sqrt_ab * x - (1 - ab).sqrt() * v
129:         x = sqrt_ab_prev * z0_pred + sqrt_1mab_prev * (x - sqrt_ab * z0_pred) / (
130:             (1 - ab).sqrt() + 1e-8
131:         )
132: 
133:     if return_steps:
134:         return x, steps_used
135:     return x

169:     Tensor

172:     gen = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(seed)
173:     model = model.to(device).eval()
174:     if c_spec is not None:
175:         c_spec = c_spec.to(device)
176:

179:     x = _init_noise(model, batch_size, device, gen)

181:     steps_used = 0

183:         if spectral_schedule is not None:
184:             t_frac = sig / schedule.num_steps
185:             if spectral_schedule.is_heat_death(torch.tensor(t_frac, device=device)):
186:                 break
187:         steps_used += 1
188:         t = torch.full((batch_size,), int(sig), device=device, dtype=torch.long)
189:         v = model(x, t, c_spec=c_spec)
190: 
191:         ab = schedule.alpha_bar[int(sig)]
192:         ab_prev = schedule.alpha_bar[int(sig_prev)]
193:         sqrt_ab = ab.sqrt()
194:         sqrt_1mab = (1 - ab).sqrt()
195: 
196:         z0_pred = sqrt_ab * x - sqrt_1mab * v
197: 
198:         sqrt_ab_prev = ab_prev.sqrt()
199:         sqrt_1mab_prev = (1 - ab_prev).sqrt()
200:         x = sqrt_ab_prev * z0_pred + sqrt_1mab_prev * v
201: 
202:     if return_steps:
203:         return x, steps_used
204:     return x

207: def sample_ddim_steps(
208:     model: nn.Module,
209:     schedule: CosineSchedule,
210:     c_spec: Tensor | None = None,
211:     batch_size: int = 1,
212:     steps: int = 50,
213:     seed: int = 3407,
214:     device: torch.device = torch.device("cpu"),

218:

225: 
226:     sigmas = schedule.sample_sigmas(steps).to(device)
227: 
228:     x = _init_noise(model, batch_size, device, gen)
229:     yield x

237:         v = model(x, t, c_spec=c_spec)

\subsection{Stage 2 — Dense Unconditional Sampling (Sound-Bank Generation)}
\label{subsec:stage2}

Given trained $\mathcal{M}$, a sound bank $\mathcal{B}$ of $n$ clips is
generated by running the DDIM or Euler sampler on the 1-D DiT
unconditionally, then decoding through the
\texttt{ClockGatedGraphDecoder}:
\begin{equation}
  \hat{z}^{(j)} \sim p_\theta(z \mid c_{\mathrm{spec}}),
  \qquad j = 1, \ldots, n,
  \label{eq:sampling}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
  \hat{x}^{(j)} = D_\psi\!\left(\hat{z}^{(j)};\;
    U_q,\; \lambda^{\mathrm{ED}},\; c_{\mathrm{spec}}^{(j)}\right),
  \label{eq:decoding}
\end{equation}
where $c_{\mathrm{spec}}^{(j)}$ is derived \emph{self-consistently} from
$\hat{z}^{(j)}$ itself (no separate chart sampling required). The bank
$\mathcal{B} = \{\hat{x}^{(1)}, \ldots, \hat{x}^{(n)}\}$ consists of
samples that are perceptually self-similar — drawn from the same frozen
manifold — yet acoustically distinct because \texttt{SEED=None} is the
default.

The bank is \emph{super-dense} in the sense that every draw lands on the
same frozen manifold yet no two draws coincide. Three mechanisms
conspire. (i)~The prior is corpus-level, not per-clip: $U_q$ and
$\lambda^{\mathrm{ED}}$ encode what the \emph{whole library} has in
common — its spectral signature — so every decoded clip is filtered
through the same stylistic identity. (ii)~The unconditional DiT is
trained on latents of the library only; its stationary distribution is
the library's latent distribution, so dense sampling sweeps that
distribution rather than an open-ended audio space. (iii)~The
self-consistent chart conditioning keeps each draw within the energy
allocation the corpus actually exhibits. Locally, draws differ because
the DiT's stationary measure is continuous and
\texttt{SEED=None} makes the sampling trajectory fresh each time;
globally, they agree because every path through Stage~2 crosses the same
projector $\Pi_q$. In producer terms: one bank, many voices, one sound.
This is precisely the behaviour a sample-library workflow wants — a
coherent palette rather than a bag of unrelated one-shots — and it is a
structural consequence of the frozen-prior design, not a tuned
temperature. A calibration caveat is owed, however: at the training
scale evaluated here the unconditional DiT has not yet learned
input-dependent structure, and the sampler \emph{contracts} all draws
toward a single latent (measured in
Section~\ref{subsec:eval_ablation}: initial-noise differences of $6.1$
in max-norm collapse to $1.2\times10^{-6}$ after 49 DDIM steps), so the
``many voices'' property is a design target and an explicit open front
of the scale-up, not a currently demonstrated behaviour.

\paragraph{Role of the sampler at preliminary scale}
The contraction measurement lets us state precisely what DDIM does and
does not contribute at this training scale. It \emph{is} the manifold
projector — the map from noise onto whatever the DiT learned — but
projecting onto a near-single-point manifold, so each bank draw yields
the model's canonical sound (the bake's ``house voice''), coherent by
construction. It is also the carrier of the heat-death clock, and that
function is already productive: the $\varepsilon$ sweep of
Section~\ref{subsec:eval_ablation} rides on the DDIM trajectory and
buys its compute/quality tradeoff there. What the sampler does
\emph{not} currently provide is spread across the corpus distribution —
that role is deferred until $v_\theta$ becomes input-dependent at
scale, requiring no pipeline change. Meanwhile variety in the workflow
comes from the sampler-bypassing paths: Mode-B latent interpolation
(Stage~3) and the \texttt{NOISE\_INJECT} training dial. At preliminary
scale the division of labour is therefore: DDIM for the canonical sound
and the stopping dial, interpolation for the variety; the scale-up
re-merges the two roles as designed.

\subsection{Stage 3 — MIDI-Conditioned Materialisation (Rehydration)}
\label{subsec:stage3}

\subsubsection{Language-model MIDI generation}
